newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Somali faction leaders still in talks in Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: Somali faction leaders still in talks in Ethiopia.

text.p: Somali faction leaders, whose forces have been battling in Mogadishu for a week, were involved in serious peace talks at an Ethiopian resort on Thursday, an Ethiopian official said.

A Foreign Ministry official told Reuters 26 faction leaders including self-styled president Ali Mahdi Mohamed and his ally Hassan Ali Osman Atto were at "an important and serious stage" of their talks in the Ethiopian resort of Sodre.
"They are engaged in serious discussions that would bring an all-inclusive solution to their war-shattered country," he said.

A key leader not taking part in the talks in Sodre, 100 km (60 miles) east of Addis Ababa, is Hussein Aideed, who was elected by his supporters as president of Somalia in August and whose forces are battling an alliance of enemies in Mogadishu.
The official said the faction leaders, who have had more than a week of talks, were discussing composition of a coordinating council to prepare for a national reconciliation conference.

More than 135 people have been killed and 900 wounded in fighting in Mogadishu since last Friday pitting Aideed's forces against militiamen loyal to Ali Mahdi, Osman Atto and a Moslem fundamentalist leader.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of the late dictator and president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
